analysis.title: US Retail Fund Monthly Commentary - October 2026
key_insights: Total actively-managed equity retail net outflows (ex ETFs and index funds) were flat m/m in October, with an estimated annualized organic decline of 8.9%. Net flows were -$65.9bn vs -$68.1bn in September.
Actively-managed US equity retail outflows worsened to an estimated annualized organic decline of 10.5% from 9.6% in September. Net flows were -$51.0bn vs -$48.0bn.
International equity outflows improved to an estimated annualized organic decline of 5.7% from 8.1% in September. Net flows were -$12.0bn vs -$17.4bn.
Actively-managed fixed income flows worsened sharply to an estimated annualized organic decline of 12.1% from 5.8% in September. Net flows were -$43.1bn vs -$21.4bn, after +$17.7bn in August.
Taxable bond net flows were -$22.3bn (-7.8% annualized) and municipal bond flows were -$20.8bn (-28.7% annualized) in October. Both turned negative in September after four months of inflows.
RBC says the weakening bond fund flows are consistent with its view, based on historical trends, that bond fund organic growth could be hurt by rising yields.

Estimated annualized management fee revenue trends for RBC's traditional asset manager coverage improved 0.1% m/m on average in October. MSCI World fell 0.8% m/m, and asset manager stocks fell 0.9% m/m on average.

RBC has seen a rough relationship between estimated revenue trends and stock returns over recent months. It says variances between the two could reflect factors outside market performance on AUM and could be a basis for further investigation.
US equity net outflows were concentrated in large-cap growth, large-cap core, mid-cap core, large-cap value and equity income, partly offset by inflows into mid-cap growth.

International equity outflows were driven by international large-cap growth, global large-cap growth and international large-cap core. Sector equity outflows were driven by real estate, utility and global health/biotech.

Fixed income outflows were driven by core bond, intermediate municipal, general & insurance municipal, multi-sector income and core plus bond. Short investment grade, short municipal and loan participation saw inflows.
APAM reported total AUM of $167.762bn, below RBC's 4Q estimate of $168.322bn. RBC calculates net flows of roughly -$3.3bn in October.
IVZ reported total AUM of $2,453.5bn, below RBC's 4Q estimate of $2,604.0bn, with net long-term outflows of -$1.0bn in October.
APAM's US retail funds had net outflows of $515mn in October (-$279mn in September). International equity outflows were $441.8mn, and Artisan International Value alone lost $214.2mn.
AMP/Columbia Threadneedle US retail net outflows were $1,268mn in October (-$1,212mn in September). Columbia Dividend Income lost $462.6mn, and Columbia Seligman Tech&Info took in $126.4mn.
Federated Hermes US retail ex-money-market flows turned to -$943mn in October from +$39mn in September. Federated Hermes Total Return Bond lost $1,304.9mn, while money market funds took in $7.1bn.

Invesco US retail flows were -$15.7bn including money market (-$16.75bn) and +$1.1bn ex money market. US equity took in $4.0bn, with the Invesco QQQ Trust at -$3.2bn and the Invesco NASDAQ 100 ETF at +$3.5bn.

RBC cautions that US retail open-end fund data is an incomplete snapshot of each manager, since it lacks intra-quarter institutional flow data and has shown inconsistent correlation with reported company-wide flows.

market_movers.rationale: RBC's $595 target is 10.0x its 2028 EPS estimate of $59.48. The last target change was on 24-Jul-2026, from $560 to $595.
RBC's $42 target is 10.8x its 2028 adjusted net income per share estimate of $3.88. The target was cut from $43 to $42 on 29-Oct-2026.
RBC's $63 target is 9.5x its 2028 EPS estimate of $6.63. The target was raised from $60 to $63 on 03-Nov-2026.
RBC's $36 target is 9.6x its 2028 EPS estimate of $3.75. The target was raised from $35 to $36 on 09-Oct-2026.

sector_views.rationale: Estimated annualized fee revenue trends rose 0.1% m/m despite weaker equity returns, but retail active equity and bond flows remain negative.

earnings_insights: APAM reported total AUM of $167.762bn for October (reported figure), below RBC's 4Q estimated AUM of $168.322bn. RBC's published estimates assume normalized equity market returns of about 2% q/q.
IVZ reported total AUM of $2,453.5bn for October (reported figure), below RBC's 4Q estimated AUM of $2,604.0bn. IVZ reported net long-term outflows of $1.0bn.

RBC's valuation basis for AMP is 10.0x its 2028 EPS estimate of $59.48 (RBC estimate). For APAM it is 10.8x 2028 adjusted net income per share of $3.88 (RBC estimate). For FHI it is 9.5x 2028 EPS of $6.63 (RBC estimate). For IVZ it is 9.6x 2028 EPS of $3.75 (RBC estimate).

macro_indicators.interpretation: Lower equity returns in October did not reduce RBC's estimated fee revenue trends for the asset manager group, which rose 0.1%.

macro_indicators.indicator: Asset manager stock returns (RBC coverage average)
macro_indicators.interpretation: Stocks fell slightly more than the market, and RBC sees a rough link to its estimated revenue trends.
RBC's historical analysis suggests rising yields could reduce bond fund organic growth. October bond fund outflows are consistent with that view.

risk_factors: Rising yields could lower bond fund organic growth.
Retail fund data is incomplete for each manager because intra-quarter institutional flow data is not available.

APAM: poor relative fund performance could raise redemptions, and a shift toward passive products could hurt actively managed AUM. More than 93% of AUM is in equity and more than 70% in global/international equity.
FHI: low short-term rates could cut money market fund yields and force fee waivers, while rising rates could pull investors from money market funds to bank deposits or direct corporate paper.
IVZ: foreign exchange exposure (CAD, GBP, EUR), counterparty risk on derivatives and repurchase transactions, and a mix shift toward passive products.

AMP: market fluctuations, low interest rates affecting life insurance, regulation of variable annuity and legacy LTC blocks, and counterparty risk with Genworth on the LTC reinsurance (50% of risks ceded).
vol_and_positioning: Retail positioning in October: active US equity, international equity, sector equity and bond funds all saw net outflows, while money market funds at Federated and Invesco showed mixed flows (+$7.1bn at Federated, -$16.75bn at Invesco).
Invesco QQQ Trust net flows by month: +$7.2bn (May), -$3.2bn (Jun), -$5.0bn (Jul), +$17.1bn (Aug), -$4.7bn (Sep), -$3.2bn (Oct).
